text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Grain crop could be Canada's largest: Prairie farmers appear to be winning race against time to harvest crop worth C$12-billion to C$15-billion.
- Justice Minister Allan Rock targets high-risk offenders: Electronic tracking devices proposed in amendments to Criminal Code.
- Chrysler, Canadian Auto Workers union reach agreement: Strike by 13,000 workers averted.
- Botha knew of killings, apartheid-era assassin says: Orders for terrorist bombings came from 'highest authority.'
- Volunteers offer their bodies to med students: 'Standardized patients' are paid to pretend to be the real thing so that doctors-in-training have a chance to get their hands on something warm.
- U.S. firm bids for Loewen: Funeral giant Service Corp. makes unsolicited proposal worth at least C$2.5-billion.

- Short sellers caught short: Investors drove up the price of Loewen Group Inc shares yesterday, putting a dramatic squeeze on short sellers and a smile on the face of founder and chairman Ray Loewen.
- Manufacturing picks up steam: July surge in shipments propelled by autos, electronics.
- WestJet suspends flights: Transport Canada issues ultimatum. Discount airline has suspended operations for an indefinite period after running afoul of federal safety regulations.
- U.S. giant bids for Loewen: But the Canadian funeral services firm is expected to fight the US$2.5-billion offer.
- Family feud sees WIC Western International Communications Inc's Frank Griffiths fired by his mother.
